entries.title: High density with a growing dependence range need not percolate
entries.statement: DRAFT proof-audit material, independent referee check pending. For every integer d>=1 and epsilon>0 there exists a stationary finite-dependent {0,1} field on Z^d with probability of good at each vertex at least 1-epsilon and all nearest-neighbour good components finite. Construct it from iid Bernoulli(q) seeds. L(v) is a nearest seed in the l-infinity ball B_R(v), with lexicographic tie-breaking, or bottom if the ball is empty. A vertex is good exactly when its non-bottom label agrees with every nearest neighbour's label. Its indicator uses seeds in B_(R+1)(v), so index sets at l-infinity distance greater than 2(R+1) are independent. Each good component has one seed label s and lies in B_R(s). For a finite dimension-dependent constant K_d, P(v bad)<=exp(-q(2R-1)^d) +K_d q^(1/d); choosing q small then R large gives the claimed density. The dependence range varies with epsilon. This is correlated site percolation and does not refute iid critical bond percolation or a fixed-range domination theorem.

entries.title: Critical nonpercolation requires uniform control of the parameter limit
entries.statement: DRAFT proof-audit material, independent referee check pending. For iid nearest-neighbour bond percolation on Z^d with p_c>0, let a_n(p) be the probability of an open path from 0 to the vertex boundary of B_n=[-n,n]^d intersect Z^d, using edges internal to B_n. Let I_n(p) be the sum of the pivotal probabilities of those edges for that event. Then theta(p)=lim_n a_n(p). The assertion theta(p_c)=0 is equivalent to lim_(delta down to 0) sup_n integral_(p_c-delta)^(p_c) I_n(p)dp=0, where 0<delta<p_c. Finite-product differentiation identifies the integral with a_n(p_c)-a_n(p_c-delta). This is an equivalence identifying the open input, not a proof of the required uniform estimate in dimensions 3 through 10; continuity of each finite-event polynomial is insufficient.

entries.title: A Peierls sufficient condition for positive block percolation
entries.statement: DRAFT proof-audit material, independent referee check pending. Let X_z be a {0,1} site field on Z^2. Assume strong rho-dependence in l-infinity distance: sigma-fields generated by any two index sets separated by distance greater than the integer rho>=0 are independent. Suppose P(X_z=0)<=q for every z and set K=(rho+1)^2. If q<=101^(-K), then the probability that 0 belongs to an infinite nearest-neighbour component of good sites is at least 378252/81240057>0. Residue coloring and enclosing bad star-contours give the bound 1-q-9t(1+t)/(1-t)^3 with t=8q^(1/K). At q<=101^(-K), q<=1/101 and t<=8/101 give the stated positive value. This uses independence of separated sets, not mere pairwise independence. It weakens the base-800 sufficient error requirement when only positivity is needed. It supplies no estimate achieving that error for critical lattice blocks.
assumptions: Strong rho-dependence of separated index SETS
Good paths use nearest-neighbour adjacency and bad contours use star adjacency

entries.title: First-reached conditioning can lower a connection probability
entries.statement: DRAFT proof-audit material, independent referee check pending. On the path o--a2--b--a1 with three independent Bernoulli(1/2) bonds, order A=(a1,a2). Let F2 mean that a2 is the first member of A connected to o in this order. Then P(F2)=3/8 and P(F2 and a2 connects to b)=1/8, so P(a2 connects to b | F2)=1/3, whereas min_(a in A)P(a connects to b)=1/2. The first-reached event contains a decreasing exclusion, so FKG does not justify the pointwise conditional lower bound. The Kozma--Nitzan global inequality P(o connects to b)>=P(o connects to A)min_(a in A)P(a connects to b) is nevertheless an equality here (both sides 1/4). This refutes the conditional proof premise, not the global conjecture.
assumptions: First means first in the fixed order of A

relations.rationale: The countermodel's statement says 'The dependence range varies with epsilon'; the Peierls statement sets 'K=(rho+1)^2' and requires 'q<=101^(-K)'. Together they distinguish high density alone from a sufficient error bound for the same dependence range.

The countermodel varies its range with epsilon; the one-arm criterion explicitly needs a supremum over all n before delta tends to zero. Both expose a missing uniform estimate. Their model classes differ and neither implication between their parent problems is claimed.
